statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail sits at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains well below the block threshold. A narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where untested hawkish September repricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: Friday's hawkish reversal closes near its low, but the weekend halt leaves tail risk at the low-band floor into the Sunday reopen
body: This assessment is made inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The verified anchor is Friday's completed session: NDX opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70%, so the close sat only about 50 points off the low of a 369-point range. That is a downside reversal, but it is a finished session rather than an extending trend, and it cannot continue while the tape is shut. VIX ended at 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range, carrying no volatility premium into the weekend. The open question is policy pricing rather than price structure. Fed Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote was read as hawkish, lifting September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to about 57-60% on CME pricing; the 2-year yield rose around 8 basis points and the 10-year 4 basis points to 4.72%. H.15 constant-maturity yields for 27 August stand at 4.20%, 4.38%, 4.67% and 5.19% for 2Y, 5Y, 10Y and 30Y. Cross-asset alignment is only partial: higher short-end yields and gold down 2.88% read as real-yield repricing, while a 14.43 VIX and WTI at 83.44 after a roughly 4% weekly decline argue against a broad risk-off impulse. Friday's internals were split rather than one-way. Semiconductors closed uniformly lower, with NVDA -4.57%, ARM -6.33%, INTC -2.85% and AMD -2.33%, while AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, META and GOOGL all closed higher; Technology fell 1.41% against Communication Services up 1.44% and Consumer Cyclical up 1.36%. Megacap dispersion of 2.47 percentage points with five of eight names higher describes rotation, and rotation is the environment in which mean reversion generally survives. Shared Finviz context collected at 07:32 UTC corroborates those latest-session internals independently and is used only as delayed cross-asset confirmation, never as live price-path evidence. None of the amplifiers that normally justify a raised Tail are present and observable: there is no measurable pullback depth, no failed retracement, no session extreme being held, and no aligned catalyst stack inside the halt. Tail is therefore held at the low-band floor of 5 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Stress at 26 reflects the untested near-coin-flip September hike pricing, Friday's weak close and a data-heavy week that opens with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs through Nonfarm Payrolls on 4 September, with Broadcom reporting after the close on 2 September. A narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday reopen, where untested hawkish repricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Confidence of 75 reflects a fully re-verified evidence set this hour, primary index OHLC, VIX, H.15 yields, oil and the seven-day calendar, held below the top band only because the weekend halt structurally removes live price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the Friday settlement and the first seventeen hours of the weekend halt. The series was uniformly green with Tail held at 5 and dominant mode normal throughout, while Stress sat in a narrow 25-26 band. Confidence decayed from 76 to 58 as the published evidence aged across the closed weekend, then recovered to 64, 72, 73 and 74 on the four most recent refreshes as primary sources were re-verified. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next 13 projected hours fall inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 26 to 29 as the reopen approaches and Confidence decays from 75 to 62 with ageing evidence. From the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen Tail is projected to lift to 12, still inside the low band and below the block threshold, covering the first live test of near-coin-flip September rate-hike pricing, thin reopen liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases to 9-11 through the Asian session and into the European morning on expected volatility decay, while Confidence recovers to 67 because a live tape would exist again. Every post-reopen structure is stated conditionally because none of it is observable now; the stated invalidations are repeated extension after failed retracements or NQ holding near a session extreme. Monday 31 August brings month-end flows and a UK bank holiday that would conditionally thin the European handover, with Dallas Fed Manufacturing at 14:30 UTC the only scheduled US release that day and outside this horizon. The data-heavy week beyond the horizon opens with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs to Nonfarm Payrolls on 4 September. The mapped policy state stays EA_ON across all 24 projected hours.
